newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sulzer nine-month orders down two pct.
newsitem.headline: Sulzer nine-month orders down two pct.

text.p: Sulzer Technology Corp said that its consolidated order intake for the first nine months of 1996 totaled 4.153 million Swiss francs, down two percent from the comparable 1995 period when orders totaled 4.252 billion.
It also said that its corporate net income for 1996 will be lower than last year.
"Due to greater losses sustained by Sulzer Rueti this year and the negative outcome of a patent infringement lawsuit of Sulzermedica, corporate income for 1996 will be lower than last year," it said.
Due to a sharp drop in demand for weaving machinery, order intake at the Sulzer Rueti Group fell by 22 percent, it said.
It said that orders received by the Sulzermedica and Sulzer Roteq groups were higher than in the 1995 period.
"They compensate for Sulzer Rueti's sharp decline in orders," Sulzer said in a press statement.
Sales by the Sulzermedica group for the first nine months rose to 845 million Swiss francs, up 10 percent.
The Sulzer Roteq Group which producers pumps and compressors grew seven percent to 959 million.

Orders at the Sulzer Infra Group were slightly below the 1995 level at 987 million francs, a decline of two percent, "and thus have stabilised despite ongoing recession in the construction industry," Sulzer said.
The Sulzer Winterthur Group had a 16 percent drop in order intake to 742 million francs, due to what Sulzer termed "shrinking business opportunities" for locomotives and castings.
